payload.name: Capture likely deceased from euphemistic absence language
payload.description: During extraction, when a speaker describes someone with euphemistic absence language (e.g., 'will never be able to...', 'I miss him/her here') that strongly implies death, use this guidance.
content: When a statement euphemistically implies a person has died without explicitly saying so, also extract the implied state that the person is likely deceased, in addition to the literal statement.
Record the inference with an appropriate hedge (e.g., 'likely deceased') because the speaker did not state it directly; do not assert cause, date, or circumstances of death.
Stop after capturing the likely-deceased state and the literal content; do not extrapolate further details about the person or the relationship.

payload.name: Resolve relative time in memory content
payload.description: When extracting a memory from a message that contains a relative time expression (e.g., next month, next week, tomorrow), resolve it to the absolute date using the message/session timestamp and include that absolute date in the content.
content: Applies during extraction: when a source message uses a relative time expression (next week, next month, tomorrow, in N days, etc.), resolve it to an absolute date using the message/session timestamp.
Write the resolved absolute date into the memory content itself (e.g., 'September 2023' instead of 'next month'); do not leave the relative phrase in the stored content.
Set world_start (and world_end if applicable) to the same resolved date so content and metadata are consistent.
Stop after resolving the expression; do not add extra details or searches.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Advice and Suggestions
payload.description: When a message contains explicit advice, suggestions, or recommendations from one participant to another, extract them as memory candidates.
content: During extraction, treat explicit advice, suggestions, and recommendations as memory-worthy. Capture the advisor, the recipient, the advised action, and the source message.
Preserve all distinct pieces of advice and their qualifiers; do not collapse or omit details. Tentative phrasing still counts.
Represent as an event or relationship memory; create at most one candidate per distinct piece of advice.
Stop after capturing the stated advice; do not infer outcomes or expand into related topics.

payload.name: Extract Shared Bonding-Activity Memories
payload.description: When a user reflectively describes a past shared activity with a specific person and frames it as bonding, making memories, or quality time.
content: During extraction, treat first-person statements about a past shared activity with a named person that explicitly mention bonding, making memories, closeness, or quality time as a durable event or relationship memory candidate.
Capture the activity, the companion, and the relational framing.
Do not require explicit fact-like phrasing; reflective storytelling is sufficient evidence.
Create at most one candidate per distinct activity-and-companion pair, and skip statements that name no specific person or activity.

payload.name: Preserve Specific Plan Details in Event Memory Extraction
payload.description: When extracting an event or plan memory and messages state what participants will try, do, or consume, include those concrete details in the memory content.
content: During extraction of event/plan memories, if messages explicitly state what participants will try, do, or consume (e.g., a specific dish, drink, or activity), preserve those concrete items in the memory content instead of replacing them with a generic label like 'date' or 'meet up'.
When the same plan is mentioned across multiple messages, merge the explicitly stated specifics into one memory record, but do not add details that were not said.

payload.name: Capture Brief Project Mentions with Full Attributes
payload.description: Use when a speaker mentions a project they completed, are working on, or plan to build, even briefly.
content: Create an event candidate for any explicit statement of a completed, ongoing, or planned project, even in small talk.
When several messages describe the same project, consolidate them into one candidate and include every explicit attribute stated.
Stop once the speaker has finished describing the project in that session.

payload.name: Capture Explicit Disclosure Recipients
payload.description: Use when a message explicitly states someone told, informed, or announced an event to named recipients.
content: When a message explicitly states that a person told, informed, or announced an event to named people or groups, record the disclosure recipients in the extracted event memory.
Only include recipients explicitly named in the message; do not infer.
Apply this during extraction so memories preserve who was told.

payload.name: Capture Stated Discovery Sources
payload.description: Use when a user explicitly states how they learned about or discovered an event, workshop, service, or opportunity.
content: Treat explicit statements of how the user heard about something as durable facts and create their own event candidates.
Do not merge the source into the main event memory; keep it separate.
Only extract sources that are explicitly stated.

payload.name: Capture Stated Reasons for Events
payload.description: Use when a source message explicitly states why an event happened.
content: During extraction, when a speaker explicitly gives a reason, motivation, or cause for an event, include that reason in the candidate's content together with the event fact.
When enriching an existing memory for the event, merge the stated reason into the memory content.
Capture only the stated reason; do not add inferred details.

payload.name: Complete Multi-Message Event Summaries
payload.description: Use when extracting an event memory from a session where multiple messages describe the same experience.
content: When one event is described across several messages, build the candidate from all contributing messages.
List every explicitly stated activity, place, participant, and outcome in the memory.
Before finalizing, scan the contributing messages once more for any named activity that is missing.

payload.name: Distinct Recurring Events and Cumulative Counts
payload.description: When a message states an ordinal occurrence of a recurring event, preserve each distinct instance and maintain a cumulative total.
content: Before applying UPDATE to an existing event memory, check whether the incoming evidence describes the same occurrence or a different occurrence of a recurring event.

Treat explicit ordinals (first, second, fourth), qualifiers (regional, international, online, big, final), or distinct world_start dates as signals of a separate occurrence; ADD a new event memory instead of overwriting the prior one.

During extraction, when a claim states an ordinal occurrence of a repeated event or achievement, add a 'state' candidate recording the cumulative total (e.g., 'Subject has now achieved N total <thing>') in addition to the specific 'event' instance candidate.

During CRUD, keep individual occurrence memories distinct; do not overwrite an earlier instance memory with a later one. Instead, create or update a separate state memory that stores the running total.
Stop when the cumulative total and the latest specific instance are both represented; do not re-enumerate or merge past instances.

payload.name: Extract Absolute Start Dates from Durations
payload.description: When a message states a relationship, tenure, or state has lasted for a duration (e.g., 'for three years'), extract the absolute start date using the message timestamp.
content: During extraction, if a message contains a duration phrase like 'for N years/months' describing an ongoing relationship, tenure, or state, resolve the reference timestamp (message/session time) minus the duration to an absolute date (year or full date) and include that absolute start in the memory content and/or world_start.
Do not store only the relative duration; the absolute date is needed for future temporal queries.
If the exact month/day is unknown, record at least the start year, phrasing it as 'started in YYYY' or 'since YYYY'.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Entity Status Updates
payload.description: Use during extraction when a speaker explicitly states the current condition or status of an entity they own, manage, or are responsible for.
content: During extraction, if a message contains an explicit declarative statement about the current status of an owned/managed entity, create a `state` candidate for that entity.
Only extract when the speaker directly states the condition; do not infer from vague sentiment or questions.
During CRUD, when a newer status update for the same entity arrives, UPDATE the existing state memory rather than adding a duplicate.

payload.name: Extract Enumerated Group Attributes
payload.description: Use when a user message enumerates attributes for multiple members of a group using ordinal or sequential markers.
content: During extraction, when a user message enumerates attributes for multiple members of a group using ordinal or sequential markers (e.g., oldest, second, third, youngest), extract one memory candidate per described member instead of treating the message as non-factual or skipping it.

Use a compact memory kind (profile, preference, or state) and link each candidate to the same subject so the full enumeration can be reconstructed; do not merge the members into a single vague memory.

payload.name: Capture Time Gaps Between Related Events
payload.description: When a message describes an event that references or matches a previously stored event, capture the elapsed time between them as a relationship memory.
content: During extraction, if a message presents an event that explicitly references or parallels a previously stored event (e.g., 'another', 'recently', 'again', 'since last time'), compute the time elapsed between the two events using the message/session timestamps and add one 'relationship' candidate stating that duration.

Also, if the current message describes an event that matches an existing event of the same type for the same subject, compare timestamps or explicit time mentions to compute the elapsed time between the two occurrences and record the temporal relationship.
Only create this candidate when both events are directly evidenced in the session; do not infer unmentioned events or speculate about intervals.

payload.name: Extract Explicit First-Person Disclosures
payload.description: Use during extraction when a user explicitly discloses their ongoing activities, personal state, or self-beliefs in a message.
content: During extraction, treat explicit first-person statements about ongoing work, study, activities, personal state (stress, health, mood), or self-beliefs as candidate memories.
Capture the exact subjects or states stated; do not expand to related topics or infer unstated states.
Record as a `state` or `profile` memory with the speaker as subject and the source message as evidence; a single explicit statement is sufficient.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Preference Statements
payload.description: When a speaker explicitly states a preference, favorite, or strong like/dislike for a specific item or activity, create a preference memory during extraction.
content: During extraction, scan every message for explicit preference expressions (e.g., 'I love', 'my favorite is', 'really into', 'X is beautiful', 'go crazy for') and create a preference candidate for each distinct item or activity mentioned.
Include preferences attributed to the speaker's pets, children, or family as valid memories; record the specific subject and the liked items/activities.
Do not convert explicit enjoyment into a recommendation or event memory; preserve the original preference wording.
Capture preferences from casual, short, or reflective statements, including those with positive affect (e.g., 'awesome', 'so fun') even without 'I like'.
Stop after capturing all explicit preferences; do not infer additional ones beyond what is stated.

payload.name: Extract Behavior-Purpose Links
payload.description: Use when a speaker explicitly connects an activity or behavior to a purpose like stress relief, comfort, boredom, or motivation.
content: During extraction, if a speaker links a behavior (eating, exercise, visiting a place, etc.) to a purpose or internal state (stress relief, comfort, motivation), create a memory candidate that records the behavior as a means to that purpose, using memory kind 'preference' or 'event' as appropriate.
Do not let a concurrent emotional state (e.g., guilt) replace this behavior-purpose fact.

During CRUD, when such a preference candidate is present, do not merge or overwrite it with a broader state memory that omits the purpose; preserve the behavior-purpose link unless new evidence contradicts it.

payload.name: Extract Comfort and Joy Sources
payload.description: Use when a message states that something cheers the user up, brings joy, or provides comfort.
content: During extraction, if the user mentions a pet, hobby, person, item, or activity that provides cheer, comfort, or emotional support, create a separate durable memory (preference, relationship, or state) capturing that source, even when the message also contains stress or negative events.
Do not merge the supportive source only into a negative-event candidate; it should be its own candidate so it survives later SKIP/MERGE decisions.
Extract only sources explicitly stated as supportive; do not infer unmentioned ones.

payload.name: Extract Completed Project Event Memories
payload.description: Use when a message contains an explicit statement that a speaker finished or completed a project, task, or deliverable in the past.
content: If a message states in first person that the speaker finished, completed, or wrapped up a named project, create an event candidate with actor, action, object, and resolved time.
Resolve relative time phrases using the message's occurred_at timestamp; do not skip the candidate merely because the time is relative.

payload.name: Extract Concrete Activity from Follow-Up Clarification
payload.description: Use when a message describes an activity vaguely and the next message names the concrete result.
content: During extraction, treat any message reporting the speaker performing an activity as a candidate source, even when the object is only a photo or pronoun.
If the following message from another participant identifies the concrete object or result, extract an event memory capturing who did what, using both messages as evidence.
Do not skip follow-up messages that clarify or name an earlier activity.

payload.name: Extract Each Distinct Claim as Separate Memory
payload.description: Use when a message contains multiple distinct facts, activities, or claims that should each be stored as its own memory candidate.
content: During candidate extraction, parse each message into every distinct durable claim (facts, invitations, interests, jokes, hypothetical plans, activities, events, achievements) and generate one candidate per claim; do not let one dominant topic suppress secondary clauses.
When a message describes an activity or event but also states a durable fact about a person (e.g., starting/owning a business, career change), create a separate candidate for that fact.

When a message explicitly mentions an item, accessory, clothing, or object used with, worn by, or placed on a subject, capture that detail as its own distinct fact, even if the message's main focus is a different activity.
Do not merge enumerated items into a single summary that expands only the highlighted one; each distinct fact must remain individually retrievable.
Stop once every non-redundant claim in the message has a corresponding candidate; do not add interpretations beyond what the speaker stated.

payload.name: Extract Event from Action Narrative
payload.description: Use when a user message explicitly describes a past incident and lists the concrete actions they took in response.
content: If a user message explicitly states a specific past event and lists concrete actions taken, extract one compact event memory capturing the event and the action sequence.
Keep all listed actions in a single memory rather than creating separate memories.
Only extract when the event is specific and the actions are explicit.

payload.name: Extract Explicitly Stated Feelings
payload.description: Use when a message explicitly states a person's feeling or emotional reaction about an event, person, or relationship.
content: During extraction, treat explicit sentiment phrases (e.g., 'I love her', 'I felt so proud', 'a sense of accomplishment') as memory-worthy evidence.
Create a candidate capturing the subject, the feeling, and the triggering event or relationship, preserving the specific feeling words from the source.
Do not skip reflective or nostalgic messages; stop after capturing the stated sentiment and its subject.

payload.name: Extract Facts from Photo or Keepsake Statements
payload.description: Use when a user describes what a photo, album, video, or keepsake shows.
content: Treat statements about photos, albums, videos, or keepsakes as potential carriers of facts.
If the user explicitly describes what the item shows, extract the underlying fact as a candidate.
Extract only facts explicitly stated; do not infer.
Do not create a separate memory for the act of looking at memories unless it expresses a durable state.

payload.name: Extract Claims from Figurative Language
payload.description: Use when a message contains figurative, exclamatory, or metaphorical language that ascribes an attribute or feeling to a subject.
content: During candidate extraction, do not skip expressive or figurative statements as non-factual.

If a speaker uses exclamatory or metaphorical phrasing (e.g., 'it's magical', 'pure bliss', 'a nightmare') to describe their feeling about an activity, person, or object, create a `preference` or `profile` candidate that captures the literal attribute or opinion stated.
Preserve the compared object or image verbatim or as a close paraphrase within the memory content; extract only the explicit claim, do not infer additional attributes.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Goals and Intended Impact
payload.description: Use when a message states a hope, goal, dream, or intended impact for an activity or interest.
content: During extraction, if a message explicitly states a user's goal, hope, aspiration, or intended impact for an activity (e.g., share stories, make a difference, reach others), capture it as a separate facet in the memory content; do not replace it with only current emotional benefits like escape, expression, or healing.
When enriching an existing memory, preserve previously stored facets and ADD the newly stated goal or impact rather than overwriting the memory with a narrower paraphrase.
Stop after capturing the explicit goal and its immediate context; do not enumerate every possible future hope or infer unstated ambitions.

payload.name: Extract Inspiration and Plan Memories
payload.description: Use when a user mentions what inspired or motivated their current or future project.
content: During extraction, treat statements like 'X sparked ideas for my [project]' as a plan/state memory candidate.
Do not skip a turn just because it contains no direct question; extract motivation and project details from casual narrative.
Resolve relative time from the message/session timestamp and include it in the memory.

payload.name: Extract Objects as Reminders of Values
payload.description: Use when a speaker mentions a physical object that serves as a reminder, symbol, or inspiration for a personal value or goal.
content: During extraction, when a speaker describes an object as a reminder or symbol of a value or goal, create a `state` candidate for the object and a `preference` candidate for the value/goal.
Use the speaker's exact wording and message evidence to link both candidates.
During CRUD, this rule requires no special handling; process candidates normally.

payload.name: Extract Past Event Mentions
payload.description: Use when a message reports that the speaker attended, visited, or participated in a past event with a time reference.
content: If the speaker reports attending, visiting, or participating in an event and provides a time reference, create an event candidate memory.
Resolve relative time from the message timestamp.
Store only the explicit details; do not infer a specific event type.
Stop after capturing the known event facts.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Past Events from Any Message
payload.description: Use when a message contains a direct first-person statement about a completed past project, job, or event.
content: During candidate extraction, do not skip assistant messages: a direct first-person statement about a completed past project, job, or event is extractable.
Build the candidate from only the stated facts: who, what was completed, and the time; avoid inference.

payload.name: Extract Statements of Personal Significance
payload.description: Use when a user says an object, photo, or item reminds them of someone or something, or has personal meaning.
content: During extraction, when a user describes an object, photo, or item as reminding them of someone or something ('reminds me of', 'makes me think of', 'means ... to me'), create a candidate state memory capturing the connection.
Record who is reminded (the speaker), the object, and what it reminds them of (person, feeling, or value) in the speaker's own words.
Treat such statements as durable personal facts even though they are phrased as effects or feelings, not as direct assertions; extract at most one memory per statement.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Plan Items Across Messages
payload.description: Use when consecutive messages in a session describe the same upcoming event or plan.
content: When consecutive messages discuss the same upcoming event or plan, create a candidate for each explicitly mentioned activity or item.
During CRUD, merge these candidates into one event/plan memory that retains all explicitly stated details.
Stop once every explicitly stated detail is covered; do not infer unmentioned activities.

payload.name: Extract Each Self-Reported Event Separately
payload.description: Use when a message contains a speaker's explicit first-person past action with a relative time phrase.
content: Treat each explicit first-person past action in a message as a separate event candidate for that speaker.
Resolve the relative time phrase against the message/session timestamp to set world_start.
Do not fold the speaker's action into a candidate about another person or broader theme.

payload.name: Extract Start of Specific Creative Work
payload.description: Use when a user confirms starting or recently beginning a specific creative work.
content: When a message confirms a user is working on a specific creative work with an ordinal or title and a beginning phrase, add an event memory with subject=user and world_start set to the message date.
Treat recent-start statements as start events; do not mark completion unless explicitly stated.
Prefer this specific event memory over a generic profile enrichment.

payload.name: Extract Family Pet Ownership
payload.description: When a speaker references a pet as belonging to their family or household (including via a photo), during extraction.
content: During extraction, if a message links a pet to the speaker's own family or household (e.g., 'my family's dog', 'our dog', a photo described as my family's pet), create a memory that the speaker had that pet.
Do not require an explicit statement like 'I grew up with a dog'; owning a family pet in the past implies it was part of the speaker's upbringing.
Skip pet mentions that clearly belong to someone else (e.g., a friend's dog) or that are generic with no owner.
Record the speaker as subject and use event or relationship memory kinds as appropriate; stop after extracting the ownership fact—do not expand into extra searches or unrelated pet details.

payload.name: Extract user-stated activity frequency
payload.description: When a user explicitly states how often they do a recurring activity, extract a durable memory with the activity and frequency.
content: During extraction, when a user explicitly states the frequency of a recurring activity (including colloquial phrases like 'very often', 'all the time', 'a couple times a week'), create a candidate memory capturing both the activity and the frequency.
Use memory kind 'state' for habitual routines and 'event' for scheduled recurring occurrences; resolve relative time from the message timestamp.
During CRUD, if a matching memory for the same activity already exists, UPDATE or MERGE it rather than adding a duplicate.

payload.name: Extract implied vacation location memories
payload.description: When a user mentions a past vacation or trip with a location and a relative time (e.g., last summer, last year), extract an event memory for that time and place, resolving relative time from the message timestamp.
content: During extraction, if a message mentions a trip or vacation with a location and a relative time (e.g., last summer, last year), create an event memory for that trip. Resolve the relative time from the message timestamp; use the country as the location if only a city is named.
Do not skip such statements just because the trip is mentioned as background (e.g., describing a photo). If the location and time are clear, extract the event.

payload.name: Location Qualifiers for Named Destination Plans
payload.description: When extracting or updating a plan memory that mentions a specific named venue, landmark, or business, include its commonly known location(s) so future location questions can be answered.
content: During extraction, if a plan memory mentions a specific named venue, landmark, or business, add a concise qualifier naming its well-known location(s), e.g., US states or countries.
Use only common knowledge about that entity; do not research or speculate beyond obvious, widely known locations.
If one location is commonly known, record it; if several prominent locations exist, record all commonly known ones, then stop.
Apply the same qualifier when updating an existing plan memory that references the venue.

payload.name: Extract Nicknames from Direct Address
payload.description: When a message contains a direct address or vocative using a nickname for another person, extract that nickname as a relationship memory.
content: During extraction, scan each message for direct-address terms (vocatives), especially nicknames or shortened names at the start or end of an utterance.
If the speaker addresses another known person by a nickname, create a separate 'relationship' memory recording that speaker's nickname for the addressee (e.g., 'Nate calls Joanna Jo').
Keep the nickname memory distinct from any event memory in the same message; extract both facts independently.
Only create the nickname memory when the addressee is identifiable from the conversation; do not treat generic or ambiguous terms as nicknames.

payload.name: Extract Offers, Encouragement, and Advice
payload.description: Use during extraction when a message contains one person offering help, giving advice, encouragement, or reassurance to another person.
content: During extraction, treat a single message as sufficient evidence when a speaker offers help, gives advice, encouragement, or reassurance to another person.
Create one event memory capturing the speaker, the recipient, and the gist of what was said, including any explicit guidance or offer topic.
Stop after the gist is captured; do not infer the recipient's internal feelings or expand into multiple memory kinds unless the message contains other distinct facts.

payload.name: Preserve Ordinal and Concrete Entity Types
payload.description: Use when a user references a work or entity by an ordinal (e.g., 'third one') or when a message uses coreference to name a concrete type.
content: During extraction, when a message assigns an ordinal or count to an entity (e.g., 'third screenplay', 'second trip'), keep both the ordinal and the noun it modifies in the memory content; do not reduce it to a generic phrase.
When a message confirms or references a work by an ordinal, look back at the conversation to identify the concrete artifact type and include it in the memory content.
Avoid generalizing a known type to a broader category; use the most specific type the conversation supports.
If an existing memory for the same entity stores a generic label, prefer an UPDATE or ENRICHMENT that adds the concrete type or ordinal rather than creating a new vague ADD.

payload.name: Extract Origin Events as Distinct Memories
payload.description: When a user explains how they started or got into an activity, hobby, or interest, including who introduced it or when it began.
content: During extraction, if a message contains an origin narrative (how the person started an activity, who introduced it, what prompted it, or a concrete start time), create a separate event memory for the origin in addition to any preference or state memory.
Record the causal source (person or circumstance) and the start time/age if stated; do not fold the origin into a generic preference summary.
If the origin names another person, also consider a relationship memory capturing that connection.
Emit at most one origin memory per activity per message; skip if the same origin is repeated later.

payload.name: Past Completed Activities as Events
payload.description: Use during extraction when a message includes a relative past-time phrase (e.g., 'two weeks ago', 'last month') describing an activity like reading, watching, or visiting.
content: When a user states they did something in the past with a relative time phrase (e.g., 'two weeks ago', 'last month', 'in January'), resolve the time from the message/session timestamp and record it as a completed event memory (e.g., 'read X in January 2023'), never as a current state, preference, or 'currently reading/watching/using' memory.
Do not merge a past completed activity with an ongoing current activity into a single memory; keep separate memories with distinct time spans and completion status.
Stop after creating the past event memory; do not expand to other activities unless explicitly mentioned.

payload.name: Extract Pet Activity Memories
payload.description: When a user mentions doing an activity with their pet (e.g., walking, hiking), during extraction.
content: During extraction, treat any explicit statement where the speaker describes performing an activity with their pet as a candidate memory, even if it appears in casual sign-off or small talk.
Record the activity and the pet name as the object (e.g., 'walks with Buddy', 'hikes with Toby'), with the speaker as the subject.
Resolve relative time from the message timestamp; if the activity is described as a general habit, capture it as a state; if it is a one-off event, capture it as an event.
Stop after capturing the stated activity; do not infer additional pet facts or unrelated activities unless explicitly mentioned.

payload.name: Extract Photo-Sharing Events
payload.description: When a message presents an object or result with visual language like 'Here are...' or explicitly mentions sharing a photo, during extraction.
content: When a message uses presentation phrasing such as 'Here are...', 'Check out...', 'This is a photo of...', or 'Attached is...' to introduce something, record that the speaker shared a photo of that item, even if the word 'photo' does not appear.

If the speaker explicitly mentions sharing, sending, or showing a picture/photo/image, create an event memory that records the sharing action and the described content (e.g., subject or creator of the picture).
Preserve the literal object named in the message (e.g., picture) — do not replace it with an inferred object such as a bookshelf, item, or possession.
Keep the sharing act within the same event memory as the other facts from that message; do not summarize away the visual sharing.
Only include facts explicitly stated; do not convert a shared picture into an ownership claim unless ownership is directly stated.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Future Intentions as Plan Memories
payload.description: Use during extraction when a speaker explicitly proposes, commits to, or resolves a future action or activity.
content: During extraction, treat explicit proposals, invitations, commitments, or resolutions about future activities as `plan` candidates.
Capture the activity, participants, and any stated method or manner; do not wait for the action to happen.
Keep or merge such plan candidates; do not skip them because they are tentative or expressed as options.

payload.name: Preserve Activity-Feeling Link
payload.description: Use when a user attributes a feeling or evaluation to a specific activity or action during an experience.
content: During extraction, if a sentence describes an experience and also states what the feeling was about (e.g., 'it was freeing to dance', 'dancing felt magical'), preserve the specific activity or action in the memory content.
Do not replace the activity with a general summary such as 'the experience was freeing' when the source explicitly names the activity.
If the same activity is already covered by another candidate in the same message, merge the detail into that candidate instead of creating a separate redundant memory.

payload.name: Preserve Concrete Events over Interpretive Summaries
payload.description: Use when a message states a concrete event with specific participants and timing inside a broader narrative.
content: When a message states a concrete event such as receiving/giving an object at a specific age or time, create a separate event memory recording the giver, recipient, object, and timing.
If the same sentence also contains a broader statement, keep that derived state only as an additional memory; never let it replace the concrete event fact.
Ensure every concrete noun phrase appears in the memory content.

payload.name: Preserve All Explicitly Enumerated Items
payload.description: Use when extracting or updating memories from a message that explicitly lists multiple distinct items, claims, reasons, goals, or attributes.
content: During extraction, identify every distinct item explicitly enumerated in the source message (e.g., separated by commas, 'and', 'or', or in separate clauses).
Preserve each enumerated item in the candidate memory content, either in one compact memory or by splitting into separate candidates; never drop an explicitly stated item.
Do not add inferred or unstated details; keep the speaker's specific wording when it captures a distinct concept or claim.
Before finalizing an ADD, UPDATE, or MERGE, re-check the candidate against the source enumeration and add any missing explicit item.
When a message contains both a challenge and a positive outcome, create separate memories for each so both are retrievable.

payload.name: Preserve Enumerated Attributes in Memory
payload.description: Use when extracting or updating memories from messages that explicitly list multiple attributes, reasons, or items.
content: During extraction, when a message explicitly enumerates multiple distinct attributes, reasons, or items, include every listed element in the candidate memory; do not paraphrase into a subset.

When updating an existing memory, if the new message adds or re-states additional enumerated attributes for the same subject or preference, update the memory to contain the complete list rather than overwriting with only the new items.
Preserve any explicit purpose or reason clause (e.g., 'so that...', 'to give...') as part of the memory content; the 'why' is part of the fact.

During CRUD, before UPDATE, compare the incoming content with the existing memory. If the incoming event is a different fact (different event, subject, or world_start), do not overwrite the existing content and world_start; create a new ADD instead.
Stop after one memory per distinct fact; do not split or duplicate reasons into separate memories unless they are independent preferences.

payload.name: Preserve Explicit Event Time in Extraction
payload.description: When a statement gives a time for an event (relative or absolute), ensure the event memory records that temporal fact instead of only descriptive content.
content: During extraction, if a statement states a time for an event (relative like 'a few years ago' or absolute like 'in 2019'), include that temporal fact in the event memory's content, resolving relative expressions against the message timestamp.

Do not let descriptive or attribute content (e.g., meaning of a tattoo) replace the event's temporal anchor; preserve both the event time and its other details in the same memory or as separate linked event memories.
During CRUD, if an existing event memory lacks a time that is now evident from a message, issue an UPDATE that adds the temporal information rather than skipping it.

payload.name: Preserve Exact Descriptive Wording
payload.description: Use when a speaker uses a specific adjective or phrase to describe someone or something in direct speech.
content: During extraction, when a speaker uses a specific adjective or phrase to describe a person, object, or event in direct speech, preserve that exact wording in the candidate content instead of replacing it with a synonym or paraphrase.
Do not replace a concrete descriptor with only a general sentiment paraphrase; keep both the relationship sentiment and the exact quoted or near-quoted attribute.
When later updating or merging such a memory, retain the originally preserved descriptive wording unless new evidence explicitly changes it.

payload.name: Preserve Explicit Outcomes in Helping Statements
payload.description: Use during extraction when a statement describes someone helping, mentoring, or supporting others and names a specific outcome or goal achieved.
content: During extraction, if the source states that someone helped another person achieve a specific goal or outcome, record that outcome explicitly in the memory content.
Do not replace named outcomes with a general paraphrase; include both the general description and the explicit achievement.
Keep the memory evidence-bound by using the speaker's concrete wording for what was achieved.

payload.name: Preserve Explicit Reasons and Motivations
payload.description: Use when a message explicitly states a reason, motivation, or purpose for a decision, action, or behavior.
content: During extraction, if the speaker explicitly states why they made a decision, took an action, or holds a preference (e.g., 'because', 'felt like', 'what keeps me going'), include both the action/state and the stated reason in the same candidate memory.
When a memory already exists for the subject and a later message supplies the reason, create a new candidate or propose an UPDATE/MERGE to attach it to the existing memory.
Stop after capturing the explicit reason(s) stated; do not invent or infer additional motivations beyond the evidence.

payload.name: Preserve Attribution of External Entities
payload.description: Use during extraction when a speaker describes what an external entity (class, instructor, organization) does, teaches, or emphasizes.
content: During extraction, preserve the original grammatical subject of the source statement; do not rewrite an external entity's behavior as the speaker's own preference.
When enriching an existing memory, retain the external entity's attribution alongside any inferred personal details.
Only merge an external entity's behavior into the speaker's attributes if the source explicitly attributes it to the speaker.

payload.name: Preserve Manner Descriptions in Events
payload.description: Use when a speaker explicitly describes the manner or process of an action.
content: When a message contains an explicit description of how or in what manner an action was performed (process, attitude, style), include that description verbatim or as a faithful paraphrase in the event memory candidate; do not reduce the event to only its outcome or associated emotions.
If the same message also contains other facets (e.g., emotions, result), keep them as separate candidates or within the same candidate only when they do not obscure the explicit manner statement.

payload.name: Preserve Qualifying Details in Expressive Statements
payload.description: Use when a speaker describes an activity or feeling with an exclamatory or emotive phrase that includes a qualifying detail.
content: During extraction, when a message contains an exclamatory or emotive qualifier (e.g., 'peaceful moments', 'amazing views', 'fun times') attached to an event or feeling, preserve that qualifier in the candidate content instead of paraphrasing it away.
If the qualifier changes the meaning of what the speaker expressed (e.g., missing 'peaceful moments' vs. missing 'moments'), it is a key memory detail and must appear in the candidate.

When later ADD/UPDATE/MERGE operations rewrite or enrich a memory, check that prior qualifying details remain represented; do not overwrite them with unrelated later content unless the new content explicitly supersedes the old claim.
Do not add qualifiers that were not stated; only preserve what the speaker actually said.

payload.name: Preserve Recommendation Claims During Memory Enrichment
payload.description: Use when updating or merging an existing memory with new evidence that explicitly recommends, suggests, or endorses an item, or expresses a different relationship than the existing memory.
content: During UPDATE/MERGE, read the relationship or speech act in the new evidence (e.g., 'recommends', 'suggests', 'endorses'), not just its objects.

If the new evidence's relationship differs from the existing memory's, write the merged content so each relationship is stated explicitly (e.g., 'A recommends B for C; A also enjoys B'), rather than replacing the new verb with the old one.
If merging would blur the claim type (e.g., turning 'recommends' into 'enjoys'), create a separate memory entry that preserves the original verbs and mentions the recipient when given.
Stop when the recommendation or distinct relationship is preserved in at least one memory; do not add extra detail.

payload.name: Preserve Relational and Emotional Claims
payload.description: Use when a speaker describes a first-person experience with explicit relational or emotional claims.
content: During candidate extraction, when a speaker describes a first-person experience (e.g., attending an event with someone), preserve the explicit relational claim (e.g., 'experiencing it with her mom') and any stated emotional evaluation (e.g., 'comforting'), even if the statement also touches on a broader theme like emotions or connection.

During UPDATE or MERGE, before applying an enriched version, compare it against the source message for any explicit experiential or evaluative claim; if the update drops such a claim, revise the candidate or update to include it rather than relying on implication.

payload.name: Preserve Explicit Subjective Content in Extraction
payload.description: Use when a message contains explicit feelings, evaluations, motivations, or subjective reactions; ensure they are captured as durable memories.
content: During extraction, treat explicitly stated feelings, evaluations, motivations, and subjective reactions as memory-worthy facts, separate from any objective event or activity.
Preserve the exact emotion or evaluation words from the source; do not paraphrase or drop any distinct stated feeling.
When a message contains both an objective event and a subjective statement, create separate memories for each distinct fact.
During CRUD, do not overwrite previously captured subjective evaluations with objective details; keep both.
Stop after capturing the explicitly stated subjective content; do not infer unstated feelings or motivations.

payload.name: Resolve Pronoun Referents During Extraction
payload.description: When extracting memories from messages containing pronouns or demonstratives, resolve them to the correct antecedent from conversation context before building a candidate.
content: During extraction, before creating a candidate, replace pronouns and demonstratives (it, this, that, they, she, he) with the exact entity they refer to, using the current and preceding messages as context.
If the speaker states that the referred object was shown or shared with a named person, extract a relationship or event memory linking the speaker, the recipient, and the resolved object.
If the preference or behavior belongs to another entity (e.g., pet, family), create a memory with that entity as the subject, not the speaker.
If the referent cannot be determined confidently, do not guess; leave the claim unresolved or skip it rather than risk polluting memory.

payload.name: Propagate Established Location to New Event Memories
payload.description: Use when extracting an event that lacks an explicit place, but earlier session messages establish a location.
content: Before finalizing an event candidate without an explicit location, scan earlier messages for a location where the speaker is currently staying or visiting.
If the event's timing overlaps with that stay and the activity is plausibly tied to that place, include the location explicitly.
Only propagate a location when the session evidence supports it; otherwise leave the event without a location.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Relational Framing
payload.description: When a user explicitly states how they view a person, pet, or group (e.g., 'pets are family', 'feel like family'), during extraction.
content: During extraction, if a user explicitly declares how they view someone or something (e.g., 'pets are family', 'my little family', 'feel like family', 'as a friend'), create a separate profile or relationship memory capturing that view, even if the message also contains event details like photos or activities.
Use memory kind 'relationship' when the statement defines a connection between the speaker and the subject; otherwise use 'state' or 'preference' for attitudes and values.
Apply to both first mentions and repeated mentions across sessions; record the view as a durable memory rather than folding it into an event memory.
Only extract when the framing is explicit or strongly implied; do not infer relationships from generic pleasantries, compliments, or small talk.
Stop after capturing the explicit view in one memory per stated relationship; do not add redundant memories for every photo or activity that merely implies the same view.

payload.name: Resolve Relative Time in Event Extraction
payload.description: Use when extracting or updating event/plan memories from messages containing relative time expressions like yesterday, last week, or next month.
content: During extraction, detect relative time expressions (yesterday, today, last week, next month, N days ago, last Friday, this weekend) and resolve them to absolute calendar dates using the message/session timestamp.
Set world_start (and world_end if implied) to the resolved date; do not default to the message timestamp when the phrase indicates a different time.
Store the resolved absolute date in the memory content, not the raw relative phrase, so the date remains recoverable.
When updating or merging event memories, preserve resolved dates from candidates; do not recompute or overwrite them with guessed dates.
For plural subjects like 'we', include all established participants in the memory, not just the speaker.

payload.name: Resolve Action Object Before Extracting Event Facts
payload.description: Use when extracting an event memory from a sentence that contains an action verb plus a possessive or locating phrase.
content: For each event or action verb, identify the direct object the verb governs; do not attach the action to an entity in a modifying phrase.
When a relative time phrase modifies the action, resolve it from the message/session timestamp and set world_start.
If the same sentence mentions both a previously-known entity and a newly purchased object, emit a separate event memory for the action on the new object.

payload.name: Role-Agnostic Multi-Claim Extraction
payload.description: Use during extraction when a message from any speaker contains direct answers, assessments, or lists of actions that should be captured as separate memories.
content: During extraction, treat every message in the session as a potential source of facts regardless of the speaker's role.
When a message contains multiple distinct claims (e.g., an assessment plus a list of actions), create one candidate per claim; do not collapse them.
For negated phrases, record the asserted meaning as a factual claim.

payload.name: Preserve Shared Event Participants
payload.description: When extracting event or relationship memories from messages describing shared activities with first-person plural or reciprocal affirmations, preserve all participants.
content: During extraction, if a message describes an activity with another person using first-person plural (we, us, our, my partner and I), preserve that shared participation in the candidate.
Include the companion and, when stated, their relationship to the speaker; do not rewrite the event as a solo activity.
When a speaker affirms a shared habit or state with a reciprocal phrase ('same here', 'me too', 'likewise'), extract separate candidates for both speaker and addressee when identifiable.
If the co-participant is unknown or 'we' is ambiguous, do not invent a specific person; record only the speaker.
When later messages reveal an omitted participant, use UPDATE or MERGE to add that participant instead of creating a duplicate event.

payload.name: Attribute Memories to Actual Speaker
payload.description: When extracting profile or preference memories from multi-party conversations, attribute each statement to the speaker who uttered it, not to another mentioned participant.
content: During extraction, treat each speaker's message as its own evidence unit: create a separate candidate per message and per speaker, and set the memory's subject to the speaker who uttered that message.
Do not merge opinions from different speakers into a single memory unless the speakers explicitly state the view jointly (e.g., 'we both like').
When a message contains a self-disclosure (e.g., 'I also have...', 'Yes, I...'), create a separate candidate for that speaker even if the message also contains a question or reply.
If the message text clearly attributes the preference to someone else (e.g., 'Tim loves...'), use that person only then; otherwise default to the speaker.

payload.name: Record Specific Product Type in Creation Events
payload.description: Use when creating or updating a memory about someone making a product line, collection, or series, and the message names the specific item type.
content: When creating or updating an event memory about someone creating or making a product line, collection, or series, always resolve coreferences in the message and record the concrete product/item type (e.g., hoodies) that the line consists of.
Do not use generic terms like 'a line' or 'a collection' when the message specifies what the line or collection contains.

payload.name: Correct Subject Attribution in Multiparty Messages
payload.description: Use during extraction when a message relays information about another participant's condition, status, or plans, to attribute the memory to the correct person.
content: Before creating a memory from a message, identify the actual subject: the person whose condition, action, or plan is described, not necessarily the speaker.
When a message relays a third party's assessment about another participant, store the fact as a state for that participant, including the quoted assessment.
If the same message contains information about multiple people, create separate memories for each person.

payload.name: Preserve Third-Party Evaluative Statements
payload.description: Use during extraction when a speaker evaluates another person's qualities, progress, or suitability for a role.
content: During extraction, create a candidate memory whenever a participant evaluates another person's qualities, progress, success, or suitability.
Represent it as a `state` memory about the person being evaluated, or as an `event` memory preserving the speaker's exact statement; link the speaker as the evidence source.
Record only qualities explicitly stated; do not add inferred traits.

payload.name: Update Existing Event on Completion
payload.description: When a message indicates completion or ending of an event already in memory, update the existing memory instead of adding a duplicate.
content: Before adding a completion/end candidate, search the retrieved existing memories for an ongoing event with the same subject and referent (e.g., same project, task, or activity).
If an existing event memory matches, apply an UPDATE or MERGE: set world_end from the message timestamp or explicit date, and record the duration if it can be computed from the stored world_start.
Do not ADD a separate completion event for the same referent; keep one canonical event memory for the whole lifecycle.
If no matching ongoing memory exists, then ADD the completion/end event as a new memory.

payload.name: Verify Duplicate Before SKIP
payload.description: Use when a construction candidate is about to be SKIPped as duplicate or already represented.
content: Before SKIPping a candidate as duplicate or already represented, verify that the retrieved existing-memory pool contains a memory that fully covers the candidate's subject, memory kind, content, and time.
If no such memory exists, do not SKIP; ADD the candidate as a new memory, or MERGE/UPDATE it into the closest related memory if the relationship is evident.
Do not treat mere topic or category overlap as redundancy; the exact fact must already be present.
If the candidate contains any new distinct fact, store it via ADD or MERGE/UPDATE, preserving source links and timestamps.
Stop after the new fact is stored once; do not create multiple near-identical memories.

payload.name: AggregateRepeatedVisitCounts
payload.description: When a message shows a person visiting a place and existing memories record an earlier visit by the same person to the same place, create or update a memory stating the total number of visits.
content: During extraction, when a message states that a person visited a place and another message in the session already establishes an earlier visit by the same person to the same place, generate a candidate memory containing the cumulative number of visits; do not expand this to other places or trips.

During CRUD, when adding or updating a visit event, search the retrieved memory pool for prior visits by the same person to the same place; if found, add a compact visit-count memory or update the existing one so the total count is explicit.
Only aggregate same-person, same-place visits; do not count different locations, do not add a count memory when no prior visit exists, and stop once the count is recorded.
